name: Airbus A320neo family
summary: Re-engined A320 family with CFM LEAP-1A or Pratt & Whitney GTF engines; flown in the US by Frontier, Spirit, American, Delta, United, JetBlue and Hawaiian.

wings: Same low swept wing as the ceo, but every airframe has tall curved sharklets
Never has the small arrowhead wingtip fences
engines: Much larger-diameter nacelles (LEAP-1A or PW1100G GTF) hanging low and close to the ground
Nacelles extend far forward of the wing leading edge
Smooth nacelle lip with a short exhaust; no serrated chevrons
fuselage: Same circular 6-abreast fuselage and blunt nose as the original family
A321neo ACF may lack the over-wing exit doors and has a reshuffled door layout
tail: Identical tall swept fin and low-set tailplane to the ceo
Tailcone ends in a horizontal wedge

tellTales: Engines so big the nacelle bottoms nearly scrape the ground
Tall curved sharklets at every wingtip
Fat engine fronts that sit well forward of the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The neo's nacelles are visibly fatter and hang lower and further forward; the ceo has smaller engines, and if you see wingtip fences it is a ceo.
The neo has a blunt rounded nose, smooth nacelle exhausts and curved sharklets; the 737 MAX has a pointed nose, sawtooth chevron exhausts and a split twin-blade wingtip.
The neo has a wider 6-abreast body and tall sharklets; the A220 is slimmer with plain wingtips and big square windows.

usCount.source: Airline fleet data (Frontier, Spirit, American, Delta, United, JetBlue, Hawaiian; planespotters.net)
